---
title: "MAE final draft process"
subtitle: "The unofficial guide to getting the Department Chair's authorization"
---

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
This is the unofficial guide. As of this writing it reflects the current MAE
process — please check with the MAE office to confirm before relying on it.
:::

Before starting, you should have submitted drafts to your advisor and
co-advisor/second reader and addressed any revisions they requested. See the
[thesis timeline](../advising/thesis-timeline.qmd) for where this falls in your
final quarter.

## 1. Prepare the materials

- In Python, initiate routing of the TRAF for advisor signatures. Both advisors
  should sign off in Python and add any comments.
- Print the "first eight pages" of the thesis from Python — cover page, abstract,
  signature page, and so on.
- Print the final thesis document in full.
- Review the printed copy. Formatting errors frequently show up only in print.
- Collect signatures in ink from your advisor and co-advisor/second reader. Digital
  signatures can be used only in extenuating circumstances.

## 2. Submit

Submit the printed materials, with signatures, to the MAE office.

## 3. Receive review and make corrections

When the review is complete you will get an email from the MAE office to pick up
your marked-up paper copy. Make any requested corrections.

## 4. Submit the revised copy

- Submit your corrected draft electronically as a PDF.
- Deliver the original marked-up paper copy to the MAE office for comparison
  against the updated PDF.

## 5. Final signatures from the Chair

- Signed electronically in Python.
- Signed in ink on the signature page, within the "first eight pages."
